summary: Sevelamer carbonate is a non-absorbed, metal- and calcium-free anion-exchange polymer that binds dietary phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract to control serum phosphorus in adults and children 6 years and older with chronic kidney disease on dialysis. It is taken three times daily with meals and titrated to serum phosphorus targets. Because it is not systemically absorbed, systemic toxicity is low, but it commonly causes gastrointestinal effects (vomiting, nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia) and serious GI events (bowel obstruction, ileus, ulcers, perforation) have been reported. It can reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), folic acid, and certain co-administered drugs, which should be dose-separated.

moa: Sevelamer carbonate is a non-absorbed, cross-linked polymeric amine free of metal and calcium. Its multiple amines become protonated in the intestine and bind phosphate molecules through ionic and hydrogen bonding. By binding phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract and decreasing its absorption, sevelamer lowers serum phosphorus. It also binds bile acids, which may reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to sevelamer carbonate, sevelamer hydrochloride, or any excipient
relative: Severe GI motility disorders including severe constipation
monitor: Patients who develop severe GI symptoms

preg: Sevelamer carbonate is not absorbed systemically after oral administration and maternal use is not expected to result in fetal drug exposure. However, it may decrease serum levels of fat-soluble vitamins and folic acid in pregnant women, so supplementation should be considered.
lact: Sevelamer carbonate is not absorbed systemically by the mother, and breastfeeding is not expected to result in exposure of the child. As with pregnancy, it may decrease maternal fat-soluble vitamin and folic acid levels; consider supplementation.
renal: Sevelamer is indicated specifically for control of serum phosphorus in CKD patients on dialysis. It is not systemically absorbed, so no systemic dose adjustment for renal function is described; dosing is titrated to serum phosphorus (adults) or body surface area (children).
hepatic: The label does not specify a hepatic dose adjustment. Sevelamer is not systemically absorbed, so hepatic metabolism is not a factor.

major: Ciprofloxacin - sevelamer decreased its bioavailability ~50%; take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after sevelamer
Mycophenolate mofetil - decreased MPA Cmax/AUC; take at least 2 hours before sevelamer
moderate: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus - reduced concentrations reported in transplant patients; monitor levels and consider dose separation
Levothyroxine - increased TSH reported with concomitant use; monitor and separate dosing
minor: No interaction observed with digoxin, enalapril, iron, metoprolol, or warfarin when coadministered
interactions.food: Take with meals; the drug works by binding dietary phosphate.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction is described in the label.
interactions.diagnostics: May lower serum fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) and folic acid levels; in trials sevelamer hydrochloride lowered total and LDL cholesterol by 15-31%.

missed: Take the missed dose with your next meal; do not take a double dose. Because sevelamer works only when taken with food, skip the dose entirely if you skip the associated meal.
overdose: There are no reports of overdosage in patients; the maximum doses studied were 14 g/day of sevelamer carbonate and 13 g/day of sevelamer hydrochloride. Because sevelamer is not absorbed, the risk of systemic toxicity is low; gastrointestinal effects would be the main concern.
